title: Sorting and trimming the products table · part 2

steps.title: Top 10 by stock
steps.prompt:
LIMIT cuts the list after N rows.
Sort first, then keep only 10.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT stock FROM products ORDER BY stock DESC LIMIT 10;
hints: Start with SELECT stock FROM products.
Add ORDER BY stock DESC.
Finish with LIMIT 10.
Write: SELECT stock FROM products ORDER BY stock DESC LIMIT 10;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT stock FROM products ORDER BY stock DESC LIMIT 10;
steps.memory_trick: ORDER BY then LIMIT = a top-N chart.

steps.title: The distinct values of stock
steps.prompt:
DISTINCT removes duplicate rows from the result.
It answers 'which different stock values exist?'
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT DISTINCT stock FROM products ORDER BY stock;
hints: Start with SELECT DISTINCT stock.
FROM products.
Add ORDER BY stock to sort them.
Write: SELECT DISTINCT stock FROM products ORDER BY stock;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT DISTINCT stock FROM products ORDER BY stock;

steps.title: Sort created_at smallest first
steps.prompt:
ORDER BY puts rows in a tidy line.
Add DESC to flip from smallest-first to biggest-first.
steps.task: Try typing: SELECT created_at FROM products ORDER BY created_at ;
hints: Start with SELECT created_at FROM products.
Add ORDER BY created_at.
Add DESC for biggest-first (leave it out for smallest).
Write: SELECT created_at FROM products ORDER BY created_at ;
steps.expected_sql: SELECT created_at FROM products ORDER BY created_at ;
